verses.text: Listen to me, you islands. Pay attention, you peoples far away. The LORD called me from the womb. Before I was born he spoke my name.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword and hid me in the shadow of his hand. He made me a polished arrow and kept me close in his quiver.
He told me, “You're my servant, Israel. I'll show my glory through you.”
But I said, “I worked for nothing. I used up my strength and got nowhere. Still, the LORD holds the justice I'm owed, and my God holds my reward.”
Now the LORD has spoken, the one who shaped me in the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back and gather Israel to him. The LORD honors me, and my God has become my strength.

He says, “Bringing Jacob's tribes back and restoring the people of Israel who survived is too small a job for my servant. I'll also make you a light to the nations so my salvation reaches the ends of the earth.”

The LORD, Israel's Redeemer and Holy One, says this to the one people despise, the one the nation can't stand, the servant of rulers: “Kings will see you and stand up. Rulers will bow down because the LORD is faithful, the Holy One of Israel who chose you.”

The LORD says, “I answered you at the right time and helped you on the day of salvation. I'll keep you safe and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and give them back the inheritance that's been left in ruins.
You'll tell prisoners, ‘Come out!’ and people in darkness, ‘Show yourselves!’ They'll feed along the roads, with pasture on every bare hill.
They won't go hungry or thirsty. The heat and sun won't strike them, because the one who has mercy on them will lead them and guide them beside springs of water.
I'll make roads across all my mountains and raise up my highways.
Look, some will come from far away, some from the north and west, and some from the land of Sinim.”
Sing, heavens! Celebrate, earth! Mountains, break out in song! The LORD has comforted his people and will show compassion to those who suffer.
But Zion said, “The LORD left me behind. The Lord forgot me.”
“Can a mother forget the baby she's nursing and have no compassion for the child she carried? Even if she forgets, I won't forget you.
Look, I've engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are always in front of me.
Your children hurry back. The people who wrecked you and left you in ruins are leaving.
Look up and see what's happening all around you. They're gathering and coming to you. As surely as I live,” says the LORD, “you'll wear them like jewelry, like a bride getting dressed up.
“Your ruined places, your empty spaces, the land that was destroyed, will be too small for everyone living there. The people who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children you thought you'd lost will tell you, ‘It's too crowded here. Give me somewhere to live.’
Then you'll ask yourself, ‘Who had all these children for me? I lost my children and was all alone, exiled and wandering from place to place. Who raised them? I was left by myself. Where were they?’”
The Lord GOD says, “Look, I'll lift my hand to the nations and raise my banner for the peoples. They'll carry your sons close to their chests and bring your daughters on their shoulders.

Kings will raise your children and queens will nurse them. They'll bow to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust at your feet. Then you'll know I'm the LORD, and those who wait for me won't be put to shame.”
Can anyone take loot back from a mighty warrior or rescue captives held under a lawful claim?
But the LORD says, “Even a mighty warrior's captives will be taken back, and what the ruthless stole will be recovered. I'll fight the ones who fight you, and I'll save your children.
I'll make your oppressors eat their own flesh and get drunk on their own blood like sweet wine. Then everyone will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior and Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.”
